title: The Bombieri–Vinogradov theorem
summary: Primes are well distributed in residue classes on average over moduli $q \le x^{1/2}/(\log x)^B$, as strong as GRH would give on average. Proved by Bombieri and by A. I. Vinogradov in 1965.
why: Level of distribution $1/2$; Zhang's 2013 breakthrough went slightly past it for smooth moduli.

timeline.title: Bombieri–Vinogradov
timeline.text: Primes in progressions on average over moduli up to $x^{1/2}$.

title: Bounded gaps between primes
summary: Zhang (2013) proved $\liminf (p_{n+1} - p_n) < 7 \times 10^7$. Maynard (late 2013) gave a simpler multidimensional sieve, and the Polymath8 project brought the bound to $246$.
why: The twin prime conjecture asks for $2$.

timeline.title: Multidimensional sieve and Polymath8
timeline.text: A new sieve for bounded gaps; the collaborative project lowered the bound to $246$.

timeline.title: The 246 theorem formally verified
timeline.text: Reported as the first automatic formal verification of the bounded-gaps proof.

title: Exponential sums and Weyl differencing
summary: Sums $\sum e(f(n))$ with $e(x) = e^{2\pi i x}$. Weyl (1916) showed $n^2\alpha$ is equidistributed modulo $1$ for irrational $\alpha$ by squaring the sum (differencing). Complete sums such as $\sum_{n \bmod p} e(n^2/p)$ have size exactly $\sqrt p$.
why: Cancellation in exponential sums is the currency of the circle method and of subconvexity.

timeline.title: Equidistribution
timeline.text: Proved $n^2\alpha$ is equidistributed modulo 1 by differencing exponential sums.

title: The Hardy–Littlewood circle method
summary: Count solutions of additive equations by writing the count as $\int_0^1 S(\alpha)^k e(-N\alpha)\,d\alpha$ and splitting $[0,1]$ into major arcs near rationals and minor arcs. Developed by Hardy and Littlewood from 1920.
key_statements: r(N) = \int_0^1 S(\alpha)^k\, e(-N\alpha)\, d\alpha, \qquad S(\alpha) = \sum_{n \le N} e(n\alpha)
why: It proves Waring's problem asymptotics and the ternary Goldbach theorem.

timeline.title: Partitio Numerorum
timeline.who: G. H. Hardy, J. E. Littlewood
timeline.text: Developed the circle method for Waring's problem and Goldbach.

title: Ternary Goldbach
summary: Vinogradov (1937) proved every sufficiently large odd number is a sum of three primes. Helfgott (2013) lowered 'sufficiently large' to every odd number greater than $5$.
why: The binary Goldbach conjecture for even numbers remains open.

timeline.title: Three primes
timeline.text: Every sufficiently large odd number is a sum of three primes.

timeline.title: Ternary Goldbach proved
timeline.text: Every odd number greater than $5$ is a sum of three primes.

title: Waring's problem
summary: Waring (1770) asserted every positive integer is a sum of a bounded number $g(k)$ of $k$-th powers; Hilbert proved it in 1909. Lagrange's four-square theorem (1770) gives $g(2)=4$, and $g(3) = 9$, $g(4) = 19$.
why: The circle method computes how many representations there are, not just that one exists.
references: Hardy & Wright, An Introduction to the Theory of Numbers

timeline.title: Four squares; Waring's problem; Wilson's theorem
timeline.text: Lagrange proved every integer is a sum of four squares. Waring's Meditationes Algebraicae stated the problem now named for him and published Wilson's theorem.

timeline.title: Waring's problem solved
timeline.text: Proved that $g(k)$ is finite for every $k$.

title: Moments, mollifiers and amplifiers
summary: Averages of $|\zeta|^{2k}$ or of $L$-values over families carry information about zeros. Bettin and Gonek (2017) showed a conjecture on mollified second moments implies the Riemann hypothesis. In October 2026 a follow-up paper used amplified moments to refine the quasi-RH bound.
why: Amplifiers single out one member of a family, the natural tool for hunting an exceptional zero.
references: Titchmarsh, The Theory of the Riemann Zeta-Function

prerequisites.title: Dirichlet L-functions and primes in progressions

timeline.title: Moments from random matrices
timeline.text: Predicted the moments of $\zeta$ on the critical line from random matrix theory.

timeline.title: Moments and the Riemann hypothesis
timeline.text: A mollified second-moment conjecture implies RH.

timeline.title: Amplified moments refine quasi-RH
timeline.text: Assumes the manuscript's analytic inputs and improves the bound with amplified moments.
